name: Campo de Los Almendros memorial, Alicante
story: Prisoners taken at Alicante port were held in an almond grove in La Goteta, about 3 km from the centre. The site was an open field of roughly 200 × 80 m ringed with barbed wire, with almost no food or water. For about a week from 31 March 1939 some 18,000–19,000 people were held here, though estimates run from 18,000 to 30,000. From here most were moved to Albatera or to prisons, and some were taken out and shot. The Nationalist army recorded 6,800 military prisoners. A campaign by the Alicante Vivo association led to a park named after the camp, opened in 2012, and a monument unveiled in 2014.
see: A small memorial monolith in a neighbourhood park on the former camp site. No original structures survive.
plan: Open public park; a 5-minute visit, near the MARQ archaeological museum and the Plaza Mar 2 centre.

boxes.text: Prisoner numbers range from 18,000 to 30,000, and deaths are estimated at anywhere from 600 to 2,000; there are no reliable records.
